key_insight: A symmetry-aware variational framework can simulate the finite-size Dicke model on both qubit-only and hybrid qubit-boson hardware while recovering the model’s critical behavior in the large-spin limit.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable route to resource-efficient quantum simulation of collective light-matter systems on near-term quantum devices, including trapped-ion platforms and classical emulators.
method: Built a variational model for the finite-size Dicke Hamiltonian on fully qubit-based digital hardware.
Developed a complementary hybrid qubit-bosonic ansatz that directly uses bosonic degrees of freedom to reduce quantum resources.
Designed the framework to preserve relevant symmetries and support both digital and digital-analog implementations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method reproduces the Dicke model’s characteristic critical behavior in the appropriate large-spin limit and was tested on classical emulators and trapped-ion quantum computers.
watch_item: Performance on current trapped-ion hardware is somewhat limited by noise, which may constrain practical accuracy and scalability.
paper_title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
